Probabilidades, umbrales y revisión huma: Probabilities, thresholds and human review in candidate screening and interview evaluation
Contexto. Las plataformas de selección u: Background. Recruiting platforms increasingly use language models to decide whom to interview, but free-text responses are difficult to threshold, audit and correct. We study an alternative: a decision model, JEV (TypeSafe, jev-1.13.0), which returns probabilities and confidence scores, integrated into Agora, Flock’s AI recruiting platform.
Métodos. Evaluamos de forma retrospectiv: Methods. We retrospectively evaluated two decisions using real data: screening 496 applications against three requirements, and judging 221 technical questions from 48 AI-conducted interviews. The main reference is a blind panel of three models from two families (Claude Opus, Claude Sonnet, GPT-5.5). We added blind human labeling of 60 CVs, with a second reading of discrepant cases and a stratified design that estimates the effect across all 496 applications. We compared JEV with Claude Haiku 4.5, GPT-5.4-mini and the evaluator previously in production, using bootstrap intervals, paired tests and threshold cross-validation.
Resultados. En entrevistas, JEV coincidi: Results. In interviews, JEV agreed with the panel majority on 80.9% of questions (95% CI 75.0–86.4), 7.7 points above Claude Haiku, 14.1 above GPT-5.4-mini and 26.8 above the previous evaluator (McNemar with Holm correction, p = 0.027, < 0.001 and < 0.001). The advantage held under all eight reference definitions tested. On unambiguous CVs, all three systems rank almost perfectly (AUROC ≥ 0.968). The difference appears in uncertain cases: against the human reference, JEV’s original policy automatically rejected 12 of 26 CVs worth inviting; at a rejection threshold of 0.05, it rejected 0, while human review increased from 32 to 136 applications. Estimated across all 496 applications, with the threshold selected by cross-validation, the proportion of invite-worthy candidates automatically rejected falls from 61% to 5%, and JEV ranks better than general models against human judgment (AUROC 0.91 versus 0.81 and 0.83). For R1, the model panel agreed with itself (κ 0.73–0.80) much more than with the person (κ 0.31–0.38).
Conclusiones. Un modelo que decide con n: Conclusions. A model that decides numerically allows a screening policy to be expressed as explicit thresholds, its cost to be measured, and the policy to be corrected without rewriting prompts. In interviews, JEV clearly and robustly improves on the evaluator previously in production. For CVs, ranking is good, but the threshold is a product decision that requires calibration with people: strong agreement among models does not guarantee that they reflect a recruiter’s judgment.
Palabras clave: selección de personal ·: Keywords: recruitment · decision models · LLM as evaluator · selective prediction · human in the loop · decision thresholds
1. En entrevistas, JEV es mejor que lo q: 1. In interviews, JEV is better than what we had. The previous evaluator marked 83/105 answers as fully answered when the panel considered them partial; JEV marked 27/105.
2. Su confianza sirve para derivar. Si d: 2. Its confidence supports deferral. When it decides only at confidence ≥ 0.8, it is correct on 91.9% of the questions it decides and defers the rest to a person.
3. En CVs el problema era el umbral, no: 3. For CVs, the problem was the threshold, not the model. JEV ranks better than general models against human judgment, but many CVs a person would invite receive probabilities between 0.05 and 0.3, and the original policy rejected them. At 0.05, estimated loss falls from 61% to 5% out of sample, with 27% of applications reviewed.
4. Que los modelos coincidan no prueba q: 4. Agreement among models does not prove they are right. Three models from two families agreed strongly with one another and weakly with the person: human validation is not optional.
Filtrar candidatos es una decisión de al: Candidate screening is a high-impact decision. A false rejection removes a person from the process without anyone noticing; a false invitation consumes interviewers’ and candidates’ time. European regulation classifies AI systems used to recruit or evaluate candidates as high risk [13], and research on algorithmic hiring has highlighted the gap between promises and what can be validated for years [12].
La práctica más extendida es pedirle a u: The most common practice is to ask a general language model to “evaluate” a CV or interview and process its prose response. That interface creates three product problems. First, the decision is hidden in the prompt: changing how strict the filter is requires rewriting instructions and testing everything again. Second, general models do not reliably express uncertainty without assistance [7, 8, 9]. Third, there is no natural place to say, “if you are unsure, let a person review it.”
Los modelos de decisión especializados c: Specialized decision models change the interface. The caller sends a structured state and a list of questions, and the model returns numbers: the probability that a statement is true, or a selected option and its confidence. Numerical outputs make the policy explicit (thresholds), auditable (each decision has a score) and adjustable (moving a threshold is a configuration change). Agora integrated one such model, TypeSafe’s JEV [1], at two points in the process: CV screening and interview evaluation.
Este informe responde cuatro preguntas c: This report answers four questions using real Agora data:
1. P1. ¿Las probabilidades de JEV ordena: 1. Q1. Do JEV’s probabilities rank candidates as well as or better than a general model receiving the same question?
2. P2. ¿Qué decisiones toma la política: 2. Q2. What decisions does the threshold policy make, and how often is it wrong against a model reference and a person?
3. P3. ¿Cómo se elige el umbral, y cuánt: 3. Q3. How is the threshold chosen, and how much human review does protecting uncertain candidates cost?
4. P4. Al juzgar si una pregunta de entr: 4. Q4. When judging whether an interview question was answered, does JEV outperform the evaluator previously in production and general models with the same instructions, and does that advantage depend on the reference definition?
Contribuciones. (i) Un diseño de sistema: Contributions. (i) A system design that turns numerical outputs into a three-way policy with human deferral and deterministic code for arithmetic. (ii) An evaluation protocol for settings without labels: a blind panel of models from two families, stratified by agreement, plus human labeling with design weights that estimates population effects from a small sample. (iii) A comparison across 496 real applications and 48 interviews, using paired tests, reference robustness analysis and operating curves. (iv) A product interpretation: the threshold as a decision with an explicit cost, and evidence that model agreement does not replace human validation.
Modelos de lenguaje como evaluadores. Us: Language models as evaluators. Using an LLM as a judge has become common because it scales and often agrees reasonably with people on text evaluation tasks [5, 24]. However, agreement varies substantially by task and data type [25], and evaluators exhibit systematic biases, including a preference for text from their own family [6]. Our panel combines two families to mitigate this risk, and we measure it explicitly by leaving out one annotator at a time; we aggregate by majority, a simpler alternative to annotator-specific error models [20].
Incertidumbre y calibración. Las redes m: Uncertainty and calibration. Modern networks tend to be poorly calibrated [3], and verbalized LLM confidence improves with specific techniques but remains fragile [7, 8, 9]. Calibration is commonly summarized using the Brier score [21] and expected calibration error [22]. JEV returns probabilities as part of its API contract, allowing calibration and ranking ability to be studied separately.
Abstención y derivación a personas. La p: Abstention and human deferral. Selective prediction studies how much error can be avoided when a system abstains on less certain cases, summarized through risk–coverage curves [4]. Learning-to-defer research formalizes when a case should be passed to a person [10, 11]. A three-way policy with a review band is a simple, auditable form of that principle, and choosing where to place the band is an asymmetric-cost problem [14].
Selección algorítmica. Las auditorías de: Algorithmic hiring. Audits of recruiting systems reveal biases that are difficult to detect without demographic data and hiring outcomes [12, 23]. This study does not measure fairness across groups (§6.4); it does provide a design in which each automated decision has a score and a threshold, a necessary condition for auditing it.
Figura 1. Flujo de decisión en Agora. JE: Figure 1. Agora’s decision flow. JEV answers bounded questions about the application; code handles arithmetic; the policy converts probabilities into three actions with configurable thresholds. Human review is an intended outcome, not a failure.
JEV expone dos primitivas. Noul devuelve: JEV exposes two primitives. Noul returns the probability that a statement is true given a structured state. Choice returns one option from several and a confidence score in [0, 1]. Agora does not ask the model to “evaluate the candidate”: it asks closed questions and leaves the decision to a policy written in code.
Para cada búsqueda, el equipo de talent: For each search, the talent team confirms a list of requirements. Each has a question, explicit exclusions, a weight, a mandatory flag and a type (semantic, experience or education). For semantic requirements, Agora sends JEV the candidate’s professional profile (experience, education, languages and skills), without name, email, phone number or demographic statements, and asks one noul question per job when the requirement must be met within a single employment. Months of experience and education level are calculated in code. Let p be the probability for a mandatory requirement; the policy is:
invitar si p > t+ en todos los obligator: invite if p > t+ for all mandatory requirements · reject if p < t− for any · review otherwise
Con t+ = 0,7 y t− = 0,3 en la configurac: With t+ = 0.7 and t− = 0.3 in the evaluated configuration. For a fair comparison, we apply the same thresholds to the probabilities returned by the general models.
Después de una entrevista conducida por: After an AI-conducted interview, an LLM extracts the technical questions asked. For each question, JEV reads the complete transcript without personal data and returns a choice (yes, partial or no) with confidence, plus a probability that the question is key to the role. In assisted mode, a key question with confidence below 0.8, or a question of uncertain relevance that was not fully answered, sends the evaluation to human review.
3.4 El umbral como decisión de costo: 3.4 The threshold as a cost decision
Elegir t− es elegir cuántos candidatos i: Choosing t− means choosing how many invite-worthy candidates to risk losing in exchange for how many reviews. If λ is the cost of rejecting an invite-worthy person and µ is the cost of inviting someone who should have been discarded, both expressed in units of one human review, the expected cost of a policy across N applications is:
C(t−) = λ · rechazos de invitables + µ ·: C(t−) = λ · rejections of invite-worthy candidates + µ · invitations of discard-worthy candidates + reviews
Esto hace explícito algo que en un promp: This makes explicit what remains implicit in a prompt: the value of not losing a candidate. In §5.5 we estimate C using human labels for different λ and µ values [14].
Es un estudio retrospectivo y observacio: This is a retrospective, observational study of existing records, accessed in read-only mode. Reported decisions are those each policy would have made on those records; we do not claim that invitations or rejections were sent to candidates.
Experimento A (CVs). Las 496 postulacion: Experiment A (CVs). The 496 applications with processed CVs (out of 518 received) for a call-center telephone sales role with a financial-sector client, using data provided by Acciona IT. We evaluated three requirements: R1 (mandatory), telephone sales of financial or insurance products in a call center, excluding collections, complaints, after-sales service without sales, and sales in other sectors; R2, meeting commercial targets; R3, using a CRM (Appendix A).
Experimento B (entrevistas). De 50 entre: Experiment B (interviews). Of 50 completed interviews with saved transcripts and evaluations, two had no technical questions, leaving 48 interviews and 221 questions.
Producción no tiene etiquetas humanas ut: Production has no usable human labels for these decisions. We built a reference using three annotators from two families (Claude Opus, Claude Sonnet and GPT-5.5), who labeled each item independently using the same input without personal data that JEV receives, a single rubric and no visibility into any system’s output. For CVs, each annotator answered yes, no or unclear for each requirement. A CV is positive or negative if all three agree on yes or no, uncertain if at least two say unclear, and in disagreement otherwise. Interview labels are yes, partial or no; the main reference is the majority (at least two of three, 220 of 221 questions), with unanimity (142) as a sensitivity analysis.
Para medir lo que el panel no puede medi: To measure what the panel cannot, we selected 60 R1 CVs through sampling stratified by panel agreement: 12 positive, 12 negative, 30 uncertain and 6 in disagreement. One member of the product team labeled them blindly, without seeing scores or panel labels, using a local tool showing the requirement, exclusions and CV experience, and asking what a recruiter would do: invite, review or discard. The sample deliberately overrepresents uncertain cases; to estimate what would happen across all 496 applications, we weight each CV by the inverse of its selection probability (Horvitz–Thompson [15]): each positive represents 3.2 applications, each negative 24.7, each uncertain 4.3 and each disagreement CV 5.7. The main analysis uses adjudicated labels (the first reading, with discrepant cases resolved by the second blind reading); we report the unadjudicated first-reading labels as a sensitivity analysis.
Segunda lectura. Para distinguir criteri: Second reading. To distinguish judgment from error, the same person blindly relabeled 12 mixed CVs, without knowing which were which: the 6 clear-stratum cases where the first reading contradicted all three models, and 6 randomly chosen control CVs. The label was repeated in 4 of the 6 controls; the 2 changes were stricter decisions (review to discard). Of the 6 discrepant cases, the second reading agreed with the panel in 2, moved to an intermediate position in 2 (invite to review), and retained the first label in 2. Thus, some discrepancy reflected labeling inconsistency and some reflected a sustained difference in judgment. The main analysis uses the first reading with those 6 cases resolved by the second (4 labels change); the unadjudicated first reading is reported as a sensitivity analysis.
Comparamos JEV (una llamada por CV o ent: We compared JEV (one call per CV or interview, without retries) with two general models given the same question, exclusions and warning about untrusted input: Claude Haiku 4.5 and GPT-5.4-mini, the model Agora used for direct interview evaluation. For CVs they return a probability; for interviews, the same three-way choice. For interviews, we also included the deployed evaluator, an agent pipeline based on gpt-4o-mini whose verdicts were saved.
En CVs reportamos AUROC (ordenamiento),: For CVs, we report AUROC (ranking), Brier score and expected calibration error against the panel’s fraction of “yes” labels (calibration), and decision rates by stratum. Against the person, we report design-weighted AUROC, agreement with a Wilson interval [18], and the estimated rate of invite-worthy candidates automatically rejected, with stratified bootstrap intervals (4,000 resamples) [19]. To choose the threshold without overfitting, we use repeated stratified cross-validation (300 repetitions of 5 folds): in each fold, t− is selected by minimizing C with λ = 10 and µ = 2 on 80% of the data, and error is measured on the remaining 20%. For interviews, we report accuracy and macro F1 with bootstrap intervals resampling interviews (questions within an interview are not independent), paired differences with bootstrap intervals and exact McNemar tests [16] with Holm correction [17] for three comparisons, and risk–coverage curves with their area (AURC) [4].
Ningún sistema ni anotador recibió nombr: No system or annotator received names, email addresses, phone numbers or URLs. This report contains only aggregate results; the CVs and transcripts without personal data used for labeling are excluded from the shareable package.
5.1 ¿Cuánto coinciden los anotadores, y: 5.1 How much do annotators agree, and with whom?
En CVs, los modelos del panel coincidier: For CVs, panel models agreed with one another with Cohen’s κ [2] of 0.73–0.80 on R1, 0.86–0.91 on R2 and 0.75–0.86 on R3; the lowest values are always cross-family pairs. R1 contained 38 positive, 296 negative, 128 uncertain and 34 disagreement cases. Interview agreement was moderate: 0.68 (Opus–Sonnet), 0.55 (Opus–GPT-5.5) and 0.44 (Sonnet–GPT-5.5).
El dato más importante de esta sección e: The most important finding in this section is different. Across the 60 human-labeled CVs, each panel model agreed with the person much less than with the other models: Claude Opus κ = 0.38 (57% agreement), Claude Sonnet κ = 0.35 (55% agreement), GPT-5.5 κ = 0.31 (53% agreement). The models share an interpretation of the requirement that the person does not fully share. Strong agreement among synthetic annotators is evidence of reliability, not validity.
5.2 CVs inequívocos: los tres ordenan ca: 5.2 Unambiguous CVs: all three rank almost perfectly
Cuando los anotadores coinciden, los tre: When annotators agree, all three systems rank with almost no errors; what distinguishes them is their behavior at the thresholds. For R1, JEV and Claude Haiku made no errors in automated decisions; GPT-5.4-mini automatically invited 1.4% of clear negatives. For R2, the less precise requirement, differences increase: GPT-5.4-mini invited 16.6% of negatives (JEV: 1.6%), while Claude Haiku rejected 4.8% of positives. Against the panel’s fraction of “yes” labels, expected calibration error on R1 was 0.093 for JEV, 0.066 for Haiku and 0.087 for GPT-5.4-mini; on R2, 0.125, 0.040 and 0.212. Claude Haiku has the lowest calibration error on all three requirements, and JEV the lowest Brier score on R1 and R2: good ranking and good calibration are distinct properties. For R1, JEV assigns intermediate cases lower probabilities than the panel’s fraction of “yes” labels, precisely where the rejection threshold operates; for R2 and R3, the opposite occurs across several ranges.
Figura 2. Decisión de la política origin: Figure 2. Original policy decisions for R1 across all 496 applications, by panel stratum. The three systems behave similarly on clear cases and very differently on uncertain ones.
En los 128 CVs dudosos, típicamente expe: Of the 128 uncertain CVs, typically customer-service or telemarketing experience without explicit financial sales, JEV automatically rejected the vast majority, Claude Haiku deferred more to review, and GPT-5.4-mini invited almost half. With the panel as the only reference, there is no way to say which behavior is correct: the appropriate action on an uncertain case is a policy decision, not a labeling decision. That is why we added human labeling.
Con la política original, JEV rechazó au: Under the original policy, JEV automatically rejected 12 of the 26 CVs the person would invite, and 12 of the 15 they would send to review. General models also struggled in this region: Claude Haiku rejected 9 of the 26 invite-worthy cases and GPT-5.4-mini rejected 7; the latter also invited 6 of the 19 cases the person would discard. With n = 60, agreement intervals overlap for all four.
Figura 3. Probabilidad asignada a R1 por: Figure 3. Probability assigned to R1 by each system, grouped by the action chosen by the person (logit scale). Solid line: original rejection threshold (0.3). Dashed: 0.05. Dotted: invitation threshold (0.7). Black bar: median.
La Figura 3 muestra por qué. Los puntaje: Figure 3 shows why. JEV’s scores separate the groups (medians of 0.32 for invite, 0.06 for review and 0.03 for discard), but many invite-worthy cases fall between 0.05 and 0.3: the model sees them as less probable than clear positives, and the original policy excluded them. Table 3 quantifies this through weighted AUROC, which measures ranking alone and does not depend on the threshold.
JEV tiene los valores puntuales más alto: JEV has the highest point estimates in both comparisons, but with 60 cases the intervals overlap and the result depends on a few labels: in the sensitivity analysis (unadjudicated first-reading labels), JEV’s AUROC falls to 0.727 and 0.804, and JEV still has the highest values. Because each sampled negative represents 24.7 applications, a few clear negatives that the person invited or sent to review carry substantial weight in any population estimate.
5.5 Cuánto cuesta no perder candidatos: 5.5 The cost of not losing candidates
Figura 4. Curvas de operación sobre las: Figure 4. Operating curves across all 496 applications as the rejection threshold moves (t+ = 0.7 fixed): the horizontal axis shows applications sent to human review (exact count); the vertical axis shows the proportion of human-labeled invite-worthy candidates who would be automatically rejected (weighted estimate, main analysis). Labels mark 0.3 and 0.05.
Con el umbral original, la política de J: At the original threshold, JEV’s policy automatically rejected an estimated 61% of invite-worthy candidates (sensitivity: 72%), sending only 32 applications to review. Lowering t− to 0.05 reduces this loss to 0% (sensitivity: 29%) at the cost of 136 reviews, 27% of applications, without changing automated invitations (35). To bring estimated invite-worthy loss to zero, JEV needs to send 136 applications to review (t− = 0.05); Claude Haiku 4.5 does not achieve this within the evaluated grid; GPT-5.4-mini needs 223 reviews (t− = 0.05). GPT-5.4-mini also automatically invites 114 applications, more than three times JEV’s count, including some the person would discard.
Con λ = 10, la política de menor costo e: With λ = 10, the lowest expected-cost policy is JEV with rejection below 0.05 (151 units, versus 247 for the best alternative, GPT-5.4-mini, and 496 for reviewing everything). Under unadjudicated labels, the ranking changes: GPT-5.4-mini becomes the cheapest policy, showing the influence of a few cases in a sample of 60. For JEV, the original policy costs between 1.7 and 25.0 times the optimum, depending on λ and the scenario. Put differently, the 0.3 threshold is optimal only if losing an invite-worthy candidate costs between 1.0 and 1.1 reviews: the original policy implicitly assumed that losing someone was worth the same as reading a CV. When JEV’s threshold is selected by cross-validation, the most frequently selected value is 0.05, sending 136 of 496 applications to review, with out-of-sample loss of 4.9%; in the sensitivity analysis it is 0.005, sending 461 of 496 applications to review, with 26.4% loss. In the main analysis, 0.05 was selected in 96% of folds: the value identified from the full sample survives cross-validation. Under the unadjudicated first reading, however, the person’s judgment requires thresholds so low that almost everything goes to review.
5.6 Entrevistas: JEV supera al evaluador: 5.6 Interviews: JEV outperforms the previous evaluator and general models
JEV coincidió con la mayoría en el 80,9: JEV agreed with the majority on 80.9% of questions, and on 95.1% when all three annotators agreed. Paired differences are positive against all three systems, and their intervals exclude zero. The previous evaluator’s dominant error was treating a partial response as fully answered: 83/105 cases, versus JEV’s 27/105. For a recruiting product, this is a meaningful difference: counting a vague response as complete inflates the candidate’s score on precisely the questions considered key to the role.

5.7 ¿Depende de cómo definimos la refere: 5.7 Does it depend on how we define the reference?
Figura 6. Exactitud en entrevistas con o: Figure 6. Interview accuracy under eight reference definitions: majority, unanimity, each annotator pair (leaving one out), and each annotator individually.
Una objeción razonable a una referencia: A reasonable objection to a model reference is that it may favor systems resembling its annotators [6]. If that explained the result, JEV’s advantage should shrink or reverse as the panel composition changes. It does not: JEV ranks first under all eight definitions, from 76.5% to 95.1%, and the previous evaluator ranks last under all of them. With GPT-5.5 as the sole annotator, the reference closest to GPT-5.4-mini’s family, JEV’s advantage over GPT-5.4-mini narrows to 3.2 points; with Opus or Sonnet alone it is 14.9 and 13.2. This is the expected trace of family affinity, and it is insufficient to change the ranking. For CVs, R1 AUROC against each annotator pair was ≥ 0.996 for all three systems.
Figura 7. Curva de riesgo–cobertura de J: Figure 7. JEV’s interview risk–coverage curve: if it decides the questions it is most confident about first, how often is it wrong on those decisions?
Ordenar por confianza reduce el error de: Ranking by confidence steadily reduces error: deciding only at confidence ≥ 0.8 covers 55.9% of questions with 91.9% accuracy, versus 67.0% on those excluded; at ≥ 0.9, it covers 39.5% with 95.4% accuracy. The area under the risk–coverage curve is 0.073, versus 0.191 for random abstention and 0.020 for an oracle that knew its errors. At interview level, the assisted-mode deferral rule sent 42 of 48 interviews to review: deciding question by question automates much less than deciding the whole interview, and that difference is deliberate.
Para los 496 CVs, JEV usó 760.280 tokens: For the 496 CVs, JEV used 760,280 input tokens and 51,141 output tokens across 496 calls, with median latency of 0.66 s (p95 0.77 s). For the 48 interviews, it used 366,319 and 13,077 tokens, with a median of 0.70 s. GPT-5.4-mini used 266,246 and 14,336 tokens for CVs (median 1.12 s per call). Latencies are indicative because the systems ran through different interfaces.
6.1 Qué significa para un producto de se: 6.1 What it means for a recruiting product
Separar juicio y política. Un modelo que: Separate judgment from policy. A model answering closed questions with probabilities lets business criteria live in code rather than a prompt. In this study, that had a concrete consequence: the uncertain-CV problem was diagnosed and quantified as a threshold problem, and its correction is a number, not a rewrite.
El umbral es una decisión de producto. N: The threshold is a product decision. No threshold is correct in the abstract. The question for the client is how many reviews they are willing to pay for to avoid losing an invite-worthy candidate; Table 5 shows that the answer changes the optimal threshold dramatically. A recruiting policy should declare that cost, and the platform should measure the review workload it creates.
La revisión humana es un resultado, no u: Human review is an outcome, not a failure. For both CVs and interviews, JEV’s value appears when the policy knows when to abstain. The relevant metric is not how much the system automates, but how much error it avoids for each case it defers.
Validar con personas, no solo con modelo: Validate with people, not only models. A three-model panel from two families, with strong internal agreement, agreed with one person at κ between 0.31 and 0.38. Synthetic references help compare systems and locate their disagreements; they do not replace a human definition of a good candidate.
6.2 Qué haríamos distinto en Agora: 6.2 What we would change in Agora
Los resultados sugieren tres cambios, qu: The results suggest three changes that must be tested before application: (i) lower the rejection threshold for semantic requirements or widen the review band, making review cost visible to the talent team; (ii) retain JEV as the interview evaluator instead of the previous pipeline, with confidence-based deferral; (iii) record recruiters’ decisions on deferred cases, which are precisely the labels currently missing for calibrating thresholds by search.
Validez de constructo. La referencia pri: Construct validity. The main reference consists of models. For CVs, we added a person, but only one, from the product team rather than the client; their judgment may differ from a client recruiter’s, and we cannot separate judgment from labeling noise without a second person.
Validez estadística. Con 60 CVs etiqueta: Statistical validity. With 60 labeled CVs, intervals are wide and population estimates depend on a few heavily weighted cases, as the difference between the main and sensitivity analyses shows. For interviews, differences against the previous evaluator and GPT-5.4-mini are large relative to their uncertainty; against Claude Haiku, the interval only just excludes zero.
Validez interna. Los umbrales alternativ: Internal validity. Alternative thresholds were explored on the same data; cross-validation mitigates but does not replace a held-out set. Interview questions were extracted by an LLM, and its errors are outside this analysis.
Validez externa. Un cliente, una búsqued: External validity. One client, one Spanish-language call-center search and 48 interviews. We do not claim generalization to other roles, languages or sectors.
Sin resultados de contratación. No sabem: No hiring outcomes. We do not know whether invitees were hired or how they performed. We measure agreement with a criterion, not hiring quality.
Los sistemas de selección son de alto ri: Recruiting systems are high risk [13]. We design them not to receive names, ages, genders or contact details, to give each requirement explicit exclusions, and to route uncertainty to a person. This study does not audit fairness across groups: we lack demographic data, and inferring it would be inappropriate. Such an audit, including hiring outcomes, is a prerequisite for using automated rejections at scale [12, 23]. In the meantime, the safest recommendation arising from this work is to reduce automated rejections in the uncertain region.
Un modelo de decisión que devuelve proba: A decision model returning probabilities and confidence scores changes how a recruiting product is built: its policy becomes explicit, measurable and adjustable. For interview evaluation, JEV clearly improved on the evaluator previously in production and two general models given the same instructions, with an advantage that survived every reference definition tested; its confidence also supported human deferral for difficult cases. For CV screening, all three systems ranked clear cases well; among uncertain cases, human labeling revealed that the original threshold rejected candidates a person would invite, and that correcting it has a review cost that can be calculated and chosen. With the corrected threshold, JEV ranked better than general models against human judgment and had the lowest expected-cost policy. The open question is not which model to use, but who defines and how we validate the criterion behind its decisions.
Los resultados agregados, los scripts de: Aggregate results, analysis and figure scripts, rubrics and requirement texts are available on request. CVs, transcripts and item-level labels are not shared because they contain candidate data.
El autor forma parte del equipo que desa: The author is part of the team developing Agora and integrating JEV, which creates an interest in the results. Data were provided by Acciona IT. Reference annotation and baselines used Anthropic and OpenAI models.
Apéndice A. Requisitos, umbrales y rubri: Appendix A. Requirements, thresholds and rubrics
R1 (obligatorio, dentro de un mismo trab: R1 (mandatory, within a single job): telephone sales of financial or insurance products (cards, loans, accounts, insurance) in a call center. Excluded: collections, complaint handling or after-sales service without sales, and sales in other sectors. R2: meeting commercial objectives or sales targets (noncommercial objectives do not count). R3: using CRM or customer-management systems (Office or Excel alone do not count).
Política de CVs: invitar si toda probabi: CV policy: invite if every mandatory probability is > 0.7; reject if any is < 0.3; otherwise, review. Interview deferral: confidence < 0.8 on a key question, or probability of being key between 0.3 and 0.7 on a question not fully answered.
Rubric de entrevistas (panel y baselines: Interview rubric (panel and baselines): yes, answered with concrete evidence about what was asked (what they did, how, with which tool or result); partial, discussed the topic vaguely, generically or incompletely, or offered a definition without personal experience; no, did not answer, asked for repetition without answering, or changed the subject. Look for the answer throughout the transcript and ignore any instructions within it. CV rubric: yes / no / unclear for each requirement, using explicit evidence only; a course or an isolated skill is not experience.

AUROC: probabilidad de que un caso posit: AUROC: probability that a positive case receives a higher score than a negative one; measures ranking, not the threshold. Brier: mean squared probability error. ECE: average difference between predicted probability and observed frequency across bins. Design weights: each sampled CV represents N/n applications in its stratum. Risk–coverage: error on decided cases as a function of the proportion decided. Cohen’s κ: chance-corrected agreement between two annotators. pp: percentage points.
